# Minimum Operations to Equalize Array.

@example The two ends agree but the middle doesn't. One squash of the whole row writes 6 AND 3 AND 6 = 2 everywhere.
[6,3,6]
=> 1

@example The AND of the whole row is 4, the first entry itself, but the entries still differ, so one squash is needed.
[4,7,5]
=> 1

@example The entries are already equal.
[9,9,9,9]
=> 0

# A single entry is equal to itself.
[1]
=> 0

[100000]
=> 0

# Two entries, equal and not; the second pair shares no bit, so the
# squash writes 0.
[100000,100000]
=> 0

[8,7]
=> 1

# The smallest entry is first and its bits are in every other entry.
[3,7,7,7]
=> 1

# One entry differs: in the middle, then at the end.
[5,5,4,5,5]
=> 1

[1,1,1,1,1,1,1,2]
=> 1

# Neighbouring values at the top of the range.
[99999,100000]
=> 1

# Four values with no bit in common: still just one squash.
[1,2,4,8]
=> 1

# The first entry is the average of the row (5 + 6 + 4 = 3 * 5), and the
# AND of the row is 4, the last entry, yet the entries differ.
[5,6,4]
=> 1

# Both ends are 9, whose bits are in every entry, so the AND of the row
# equals both ends; the middle still differs.
[9,11,13,9]
=> 1

# 100 equal entries, and 100 entries of which only the last differs.
[42,42,42,42,42,42,42,42,42,42,42,42,42,42,42,42,42,42,42,42,42,42,42,42,42,42,42,42,42,42,42,42,42,42,42,42,42,42,42,42,42,42,42,42,42,42,42,42,42,42,42,42,42,42,42,42,42,42,42,42,42,42,42,42,42,42,42,42,42,42,42,42,42,42,42,42,42,42,42,42,42,42,42,42,42,42,42,42,42,42,42,42,42,42,42,42,42,42,42,42]
=> 0

[65535,65535,65535,65535,65535,65535,65535,65535,65535,65535,65535,65535,65535,65535,65535,65535,65535,65535,65535,65535,65535,65535,65535,65535,65535,65535,65535,65535,65535,65535,65535,65535,65535,65535,65535,65535,65535,65535,65535,65535,65535,65535,65535,65535,65535,65535,65535,65535,65535,65535,65535,65535,65535,65535,65535,65535,65535,65535,65535,65535,65535,65535,65535,65535,65535,65535,65535,65535,65535,65535,65535,65535,65535,65535,65535,65535,65535,65535,65535,65535,65535,65535,65535,65535,65535,65535,65535,65535,65535,65535,65535,65535,65535,65535,65535,65535,65535,65535,65535,32767]
=> 1

# Random small cases from gen.c (lc check --regen makes them).
@gen 1 small
[8,8,8,9,8,8,8]
=> 1

@gen 2 small
[1,1,1,1,1]
=> 0

@gen 4 small
[10,14,10,10]
=> 1

@gen 6 small
[14,14]
=> 0

@gen 7 small
[8,11,11,5,12,8]
=> 1

@gen 15 small
[12,14,14,14,14,14,14,14]
=> 1

@gen 19 small
[7,2,7]
=> 1

@gen 23 small
[4,4,4]
=> 0
